provenance.sourceText: Art. 41. 1. Stawka podatku wynosi 22 %, z zastrzeżeniem ust. 2–12c, art. 83, art. 119 ust. 7, art. 120 ust. 2 i 3, art. 122 i art. 129 ust. 1. — Art. 146ef. 1. W okresie od dnia 1 stycznia 2024 r. do końca roku, w którym suma wydatków wymienionych w art. 40 ust. 1 pkt 2 ustawy z dnia 11 marca 2022 r. o obronie Ojczyzny [...] określonych na ten rok w ustawie budżetowej [...] jest wyższa niż 3 % wartości produktu krajowego brutto [...]: 1) stawka podatku, o której mowa w art. 41 ust. 1 i 13, art. 109 ust. 2, art. 110, art. 120 ust. 3a i art. 138i ust. 4, wynosi 23 %;

notes: PROVENANCE REPLACED (2026-09-13), rate unchanged (23%): this entry used to cite the HTTP JSON response body of the European Commission's Taxes in Europe Database (TEDB, DG TAXUD) — an official but non-statutory source, consulted 2026-09-01. The repository now holds the statute itself, quoted verbatim by vat-rates/data/pl.json's own 'pl-standard' entry: Ustawa z dnia 11 marca 2004 r. o podatku od towarów i usług, art. 41 ust. 1 together with art. 146ef ust. 1 pkt 1), read live on 2026-09-13 in the tekst jednolity PDF (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 775) at https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/DU/2025/775/D2025000077501.pdf (see that file's entry and its own notes for the full retrieval method — curl -L then pdftotext -layout, not a fetch-summary). The `sourceText` and `sourceCheckedAt` above are copied byte-for-byte from that entry, never retyped or translated. THE RATE ACTUALLY IN FORCE IS 23%, AND IT IS ART. 146EF THAT PRODUCES IT, NOT ART. 41 ALONE: art. 41 ust. 1 sets a BASE rate of 22%; art. 146ef ust. 1 pkt 1) raises it to 23% for as long as an annual conditional test tied to defence spending as a share of GDP is met — a test that vat-rates/data/pl.json's own notes record as having been met without interruption since 2024-01-01. This note must not be read as saying art. 41 by itself yields 23% — it does not, it yields 22%; the 23% actually charged today is art. 146ef overriding that 22% base, and the sourceText above quotes both provisions together for exactly that reason. Both citations (the TEDB reading and the statute) agree on the same figure (23%); nothing about the rate changed, only which source is cited — a statute a reader can check beats a reproduced JSON payload. Consumer note (unchanged from the prior citation): this table exists to unblock `documents/tax/tax-engine.ts#ossDestinationVat` (per `resolve-invoice-tax.ts`'s own header, "OSS with no destination rate table"), which reads only `dest.standardRate` — never `reducedRates` — and `DocumentLine` (`documents/tax/types.ts`) carries no per-line product category a reduced rate could even be selected against; that is why reducedRates are still deliberately not modeled here.
